subject: Oceanography
title: Abyssal Plains
description: A quick win: understand Abyssal Plains.

hook.text: The flattest places on Earth aren't deserts or salt flats—they're 4,000 meters underwater.

buildup.text: Abyssal plains cover about 50% of Earth's surface—vast, flat expanses of deep ocean floor.

discovery.text: They're flat because fine sediment rains down for millions of years, burying all the bumps.

twist.text: Despite seeming lifeless, abyssal plains host worms, sea cucumbers, and bacteria in the sediment.

climax.text: Some abyssal plains are dotted with manganese nodules—metal-rich lumps that grow 1 mm per million years.

punchline.text: The ocean's flattest floors are its least explored places.

quiz.question: Why are abyssal plains so flat?
